_source.what: Measured fish proportions, hand-typed from docs/fish-shape-research.md. MEDIANS ONLY, typed by hand -- facts, not a database -- because FishBase is explicitly non-commercial and FishShapes contradicts itself between CC0 and CC BY-NC. docs/fish-shape-research.md section 4 records that rejection and forge/language.py already carries hand-typed medians on the same basis. NOTHING here is a redistribution of either dataset.
_source.class ratios: docs/fish-shape-research.md section 1. Computed from FishShapes v1 (16,523 specimens) joined by name to FishBase's own shape classification, a 93% join; independently confirmed by FISHMORPH (8,342 species) to within about 10% and by Infinigen's hand-authored templates.
_source.landmarks: docs/fish-shape-research.md section 2, 'Fin positions, as a fraction of standard length', computed from 7,452 landmarked FishBase specimens. p10 and p90 are carried beside the median because the spread is the point: a single median applied to 106 species is the exact defect docs/reference-fitting-research.md found in quad.leg_thick.
_source.all-teleost: n = 16,430. length:depth 3.77, depth over standard length 0.27, depth:width 1.72, head depth over body depth 0.62, caudal peduncle depth over body depth 0.34.
_source.WHAT IS COMPARED TO WHAT: fish.depth_ratio is depth over fish.length_m, and fish.length_m is the BODY length before the caudal fin is added (forge/fish.py: nb = round(length_v), then xtail = margin + lc). That is standard length, which is what FishShapes and the landmark table use. fish.width_ratio is width over DEPTH, so it compares to 1/(depth:width). fish.peduncle is the depth at t=1 as a fraction of full depth, which is the caudal peduncle depth over body depth. fish.depth_at, fish.dorsal_start and fish.head_frac are all fractions of standard length measured from the nose, which is the landmark table's own convention.
_source.NOT COMPARED, AND WHY: fish.snout is the depth at the very tip of the nose, NOT head depth at the operculum, so the 0.62 head-depth median does not apply to it and is not used. The anal fin's start is derived in forge/fish.py (a0 = 1 - anal_len - 0.06) rather than authored, so there is no row to fit; the landmark median for the anal origin is recorded below for a future pass and is not scored. Cetaceans are mammals and none of these numbers apply to them.
_source.classes are assigned BY HAND: Every species below was placed in a FishBase-style shape class by hand; tools/refshape.py prints the unassigned rather than defaulting them.

depressiform._why: FishBase's four-class table HAS NO DEPRESSIFORM ROW and this library has nine depressiform species. They were first placed in short-deep because that is the class whose length:depth number they resemble -- and that is exactly backwards. A short-deep fish is COMPRESSIFORM: deep top-to-bottom and narrow across. A ray or a flatfish is the opposite: shallow and wide. Fitting a manta ray to the short-deep band raised its depth from 0.10 to 0.16 of its length, which is a disc stood on its edge. There is no reference for these nine here, so they are reported as unmeasured and never fitted. FishShapes v1 is the one source that carries body WIDTH and would settle them; it is the one this project refused on licence.

_class_corrections: wels-catfish, stone-loach and small-spotted-catshark were first hand-assigned eel-like and are elongated. The tell was the fit: eel-like asks for a length:depth of at least 10.3, which would have taken a wels catfish -- a fish with a broad flat head and an eel-like tail -- to a tenth of its length in depth. All three sit inside the elongated band as authored and now move nothing.
